title: Daycare Waitlist Fee Scout
oneLiner: First-time parents track daycare waitlist fees, tour notes, openings, and backup coverage before a return-to-work date collapses.
theme: 외로움 / 자산 방어 - working-parent anxiety, childcare scarcity, and career continuity.

phaseA.label: Practical / Commercial
phaseA.targetUser: First-time parents and dual-income families trying to secure infant or toddler daycare before parental leave ends.
phaseA.keyUx: Parent enters target start date, centers, waitlist fees, tour notes, age-room openings, commute, and backup caregivers; the app ranks which centers need calls, deposits, or fallback plans.
requiredUiSections: Center pipeline with waitlist position, fee paid, age room, and tour status
Backup care coverage map for grandparents, nanny share, and part-time care
Decision board for hold, chase, deposit, or abandon
phaseA.spreadTrigger: Parents share the center ranking with partners and local parent chats because openings are time-sensitive.
phaseA.stitchPrompt: Build a production-grade web app prototype called "Daycare Waitlist Fee Scout" for first-time parents tracking daycare waitlist fees, tour notes, openings, and backup coverage before a return-to-work date collapses. The first screen must be a working parent planning console with a return-to-work countdown, center pipeline, application-fee ledger, callback script builder, backup care coverage map, commute comparison, and decision board. Use realistic sample data: 74 days until work return, six centers, two $125 waitlist fees, one year-plus waitlist, infant room opening in August, grandparent backup only Tuesdays, and two centers needing follow-up calls. Design direction: use the calm-consumer profile with low-stress family planning cards, gentle progress states, friendly but compact forms, and one soft teal accent for the next call. Do not make a marketing landing page; the first screen must be the working app.
